summary.oneLiner: Revenue declined due to the natural end of 3 long-running TV shows and delayed movie releases, but the company is rebuilding its pipeline with a strong order book in B2B digital and 4 presold films launching in FY27, positioning digital and film as future profit drivers.

one-line thesis: Revenue declined due to the natural end of 3 long-running TV shows and delayed movie releases, but the company is rebuilding its pipeline with a strong order book in B2B digital and 4 presold films launching in FY27, positioning digital and film as future profit drivers.
financial scorecard: Revenue: -66% YoY (INR48.8cr vs INR144cr); EBITDA: -INR4.3cr (improving from -INR8.8cr in Q4FY25); PAT (reported): -INR4.9cr; PAT (normalized): -INR4.9cr (no major one-offs); Order book: INR300cr (B2B digital); Net debt: INR137cr cash reserve (net cash position)
guidance: Revenue growth: Expected upside from Q1FY27; Margin: Film margins to be high due to 85-90% presales; Order inflow: INR300cr B2B digital order book growing; Capex/commissioning: INR150-175cr for films, INR20-25cr for digital working capital
order book & pipeline: INR300cr in B2B digital content orders (Netflix: INR250cr+, Zee Studios: INR42cr, Amazon/Sony/Star: incremental)
segment / subsidiary detail: Digital: 13% of Q2 revenue, 11M active subs on Kutingg, 400M YouTube views; TV: 77% revenue, 131 hrs produced, 4 shows running, episodic revenue at INR24-25L/hr; Film: 10% revenue, 3 films in production (Vrusshabha, Bhoot Bangla, Vvan), 85-90% cost recovered via presales
growth verticals / optionality: Balaji Studio (independent creator ecosystem), AstroVani (astrology app), AI-generated content on Kutingg, expansion into regional OTT partnerships (ETV, Aha), music rights monetization
margins & cost dynamics: TV: 30% direct variable margin at INR24-25L/hr revenue; Film: 100% profit margin post-presales (e.g., Bhoot Bangla fully presold); Digital: low incremental cost for AstroVani/Kutingg, monetization via ads/subs
capex / expansion: INR150-175cr for motion pictures; INR20-25cr for digital working capital; no capex for TV; AstroVani/Kutingg use existing infrastructure with no incremental capex
capital allocation: INR131cr raised: INR65cr to films, INR33cr to music/digital rights, INR32.5cr to corporate purposes; cash reserves untouched as of Q2FY26; prioritizing IP-led growth in film and digital over TV
risks & watch-items: TV revenue pressure from broadcaster cost cuts; high SVOD churn (65-70%); delayed monetization of digital order book until FY27; regulatory risk to apps (past ALTT ban); reliance on presales for film profitability
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes rebuilding pipeline, strong presales, and digital transformation; tone is forward-looking with focus on FY27 inflection
non-obvious takeaways: The INR117cr GST input credit and INR100cr brought-forward losses will eliminate tax payments for 4-5 years, effectively boosting net cash flow despite reported losses

themes.title: Media, entertainment & out-of-home advertising
themes.need: Digital-content, music-IP licensing and an advertising-recovery cycle underpin media - TIPSMUSIC on music IP; ZEEL/ENIL/RADIOCITY/BTML on broadcast/content; HTMEDIA/DBCORP/HMVL on print + digital; SIGNPOST/BRIGHT-tier and UFO on OOH/cinema. Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
themes.driver: Festive ad-spend recovery; music-licensing/streaming monetization; OOH inventory uptake.
